meta.productionModelRationale: Only variant B_shrunk improves out-of-sample margin accuracy over both baselines with a one-sided p < 0.05. C_shrunk_recalibrated has a better point estimate but its bootstrap interval includes zero. A_naive is worse than no model.
meta.honestyNote: Model outputs are COMPUTED FROM OFFICIAL DATA, not observed market prices. No column in this file contains a bookmaker line: no official NFL source publishes betting prices, so market columns are left blank and flagged.

correlations.pair: home points vs away points (same game)
correlations.whyItMatters: Sets the sign and size of same-game correlation. A negative value means one team's scoring suppresses the other's, so a same-game parlay of two overs (or a side and the over) is not an independent product.
Both legs share the home team's scoring, so this is mechanically positive. It is the floor for any same-game total parlay correlation.
Same mechanic as C02 from the road side; used to bound same-game combination prices.
Tests whether blowouts inflate totals. If large, a 'favourite + over' parlay is structurally correlated.

correlations.pair: team margin in week N vs team margin in week N+1
correlations.whyItMatters: The momentum test. A value near zero means last week's result carries no information, which is the statistical definition of the luck component.

correlations.pair: points for per game vs win percentage
correlations.whyItMatters: How much of the standings is explained by scoring alone.

correlations.pair: points against per game vs win percentage
correlations.whyItMatters: Defensive contribution to the standings; expected to be negative.

correlations.pair: net points per game vs win percentage
correlations.whyItMatters: The single best simple standings predictor from official data; the baseline every strategy must beat.

correlations.pair: Pythagorean expectation vs actual win percentage
correlations.whyItMatters: The gap between this and 1.00 is the size of the luck component in the standings.

correlations.pair: points for vs points against (same team)
correlations.whyItMatters: Whether strong offences and strong defences travel together. Drives whether 'team total over + opponent total under' combinations are really independent.
